title: Legal redline notes - NDA & SOW (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self - contract redline points (working list)

Context: early-stage SOW + NDA for small enterprise pilot (Acme Health). They asked to use their redline; a few high-risk clauses to flag and propose fallback language.

Priority negotiation objectives:
- Keep liability cap to fees paid in 12 months (counterparty requests unlimited / higher). Prefer: aggregate cap = fees paid in prior 12 months (or $500k floor for enterprise).
- Mutual indemnification for IP and third-party claims; carve out for gross negligence / willful misconduct.
- Narrow confidentiality carveouts so we can use anonymized learnings for product improvements (they want overly broad perpetual restrictions). Proposal: allow aggregated, de-identified product usage metrics for internal improvement; still prohibit re-disclosure of raw customer data.
- Data protection & security: ensure we are not taking open-ended processing liability. Add requirement: customer provides lawful basis, owns customer data, we process only per documented instructions. Maintain subprocessors list & 30-day notice.
- Audit rights: they want audit every 3 months; counter: quarterly with notice + auditor NDA + scope limited to SOC-level controls or specific security obligations. Prefer annual or triggered audits.
- Export controls & sanctions: add standard mutual compliance language.
- Termination for convenience: limit to 30 days notice and pro-rate fees for committed capacity. If they demand 90 days with no payment, push back.
- Warranty disclaimers: keep as-is (AS-IS) but ensure carveout for gross negligence & willful misconduct.
- Service Levels / SLA credits: they propose large credits (100%) for downtime. We should cap credits to monthly fees for affected services and require meaningful reproduction steps.
- IP ownership: we must retain ownership of the platform and models; customer owns customer data and customer-specific outputs if contract says so. Avoid assignment of our background IP. For custom model work, consider license-back or joint-owned deliverable clause.
- Injunctive relief: they want ability to get injunctive relief for IP — ok if mutual and limited to confidentiality/IP only.
- Limitation of liability exceptions: carve out for bodily injury/fraud and for a narrow data breach indemnity where we demonstrate breach caused by us.
- Insurance: require evidence of insurance (cyber, tech E&O) at limits consistent with similar deals.

Suggested redline snippets (quick copy-paste):
- Liability Cap: "Except for liability arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or a party's indemnification obligations, each party's aggregate liability to the other arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer to Provider under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
- Data Processing: "Provider will process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, implement commercially reasonable security measures, and engage Subprocessors only after providing Customer with notice. Provider shall comply with applicable data protection laws."
- Audit: "Customer may conduct one audit per calendar year upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, limited to the Provider's security controls relevant to Customer Data processing; any auditor shall be subject to Provider's confidentiality obligations and shall not be a competitor of Provider."

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Sales asked if we should accept customer-specified subprocessors list (they have named 3 cloud vendors). Legal preference: we provide our subprocessors and accept their objection rights for named sensitive subprocessors.
- Need to confirm whether this pilot includes Dedicated deployment (customer mentioned private instance). If Dedicated, push stronger SLAs and support response times; also talk about KMS/HSM management and key custody.
- Pricing attach: ensure SOW includes clear acceptance criteria & milestone-based payments to avoid long tail disputes.

Risks to highlight for negotiation:
- Unlimited liability requests (push to cap).
- Broad IP assignment (we must not assign core models/platform).
- Overbroad audit / data access requests.
- Perpetual confidentiality prevents product learning / model improvements.

Tactical playbook for negotiation:
1) Triage: accept small, nonmaterial edits quickly to maintain momentum.
2) Hold firm on liability cap and IP ownership — flag these as redlines and escalate to Sales Director if customer pushes.
3) Offer tradeoffs: if customer wants lower cap, require higher fees or increased insurance limits.
4) For data use: offer a clear carveout for aggregated/anonymous telemetry; if they resist, propose a timeboxed embargo (e.g., cannot use for 12 months after pilot) as compromise.
5) Document all agreed changes in SOW change log, and attach final signed redlines to contract folder.

Notes / reminders:
- Link to standard NDA: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LEGAL/Standard+NDA+and+SOW+templates
- Jira: LEG-438 tracks template updates (add narrow audit clause).
- Check with infra about Dedicated deployment costs / capacity commitments (ENG-2217).

Quick checklist before next call:
- Prepare two negotiation options: (A) standard cap = fees in 12 months; (B) reduced cap in exchange for higher fees/insurance.
- Draft counter-suggestions for audit frequency + scope.
- Confirm whether customer expects any IP assignment for deliverables.
- Add final SOW acceptance criteria and milestone schedule.

Random todo: remind Sales to share the customer's redline in Word format (so Legal can use compare).

---
